However, neither passage addresses the performance of traditional vs. disorder-inclusive predictive models, leaving the core premise about model improvement unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Severe lattice distortions in HEAs reduce phonon mean free path and increase phonon scattering, leading to low intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Force-constant fluctuations in multi-element alloys (e.g., FeCoCrMnNi) are substantial (20–50%) and contribute to phonon attenuation.
Traditional models that neglect disorder effects (force-constant fluctuations, lattice distortions) are less accurate for predicting phonon thermal conductivity in HEAs.
Incorporating descriptors of lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations into a predictive model will improve identification of low-thermal-conductivity HEAs.
